facts.text: I am looking for new dance studios in the city that offer classes in afrobeat and house dance.
I have been dancing for a while.
I took a break from dancing for a few years.
I recently got back into dancing.
I am enjoying the energy and vibe of Afrobeat right now.
I love how Afrobeat is a fusion of different styles and rhythms.
I have listened to Fela Kuti's music before.
I have not explored much of the other artists besides Fela Kuti.
I am interested in the energy of the music and how it makes me want to move.
I enjoy the challenge of learning the steps and rhythms.
I have been really enjoying learning the Azonto dance style.
Azonto is from Ghana.
I am trying to master a move called the "Azonto bump".
The "Azonto bump" is about hip movement and isolations.
I have been working on my polyrhythms.
I am trying to get my arms and legs to move independently to different drum patterns.
I have not had a chance to perform or dance with a group yet.
I am taking classes at a local studio.
The instructor at my local studio is planning to put together a performance for an upcoming cultural festival.
I am excited to be a part of the upcoming cultural festival performance.
Azonto originated in Ghana as a way to communicate and express oneself through dance.
Azonto is a very social dance style often performed at parties and celebrations.
Azonto is closely tied to the Ga people of Ghana.
Azonto is a way to preserve and celebrate Ga cultural heritage.
I am interested in learning more about the cultural context of Azonto and other African dance styles.
I am looking for recommendations for documentaries, books, or online resources about Azonto and other African dance styles.
